_meta.design: 30 scenarios stratified by trait-divergence (how much the ideal response depends on WHO the person is). HIGH = charged/personal/decisional, fit-style strongly determines the right reply; LOW = neutral/factual, persona barely moves the ideal answer; MED = in between. H5 predicts the correct>opposite gap is monotone in this stratum. Seeds expanded to natural first-person user messages.

scenarios.seed: I got an offer to leave my stable senior role to co-found a startup with an ex-colleague. Equity, no salary for a year, my partner is anxious. Deciding this week.
My closest friend told me something I said hurt them deeply, and I genuinely don't think I did anything wrong. I have to reply to their message tonight.
I think I have to let go of someone on my team who's well-liked but consistently underperforming. I keep putting off the conversation.
I've been offered a promotion that means managing people for the first time, but I'd lose the hands-on work I love. I have to answer by Friday.
My aging parent wants to move in with us. My spouse is hesitant and I feel torn between obligation and our own family's needs.
I poured six months into a project and just got feedback that it fundamentally doesn't work. I don't know whether to salvage or scrap it.
I'm thinking of confronting a mentor who took more credit than they deserved for my work. It could damage a relationship I value.
We're deciding whether to take on significant debt to buy a house at the top of our budget in a market that might be peaking.
A recruiter offered me a role at a competitor for 40% more. I like my current team and just got handed a big project. I have a week to respond.
I've been masking burnout for months and my work is slipping. I'm scared that if I tell my manager I'll be seen as unreliable.
I want to start strength training but I'm overwhelmed by conflicting advice online. Where should I actually begin?
I'm preparing for a salary negotiation next week and I'm not sure how aggressive to be or how to frame my ask.
I keep procrastinating on a side project I say I care about. I don't know if it's the project or me.
I have to give critical feedback to a peer on a draft and I want it to actually land without blowing up the working relationship.
I'm choosing between two apartments — one cheaper and further out, one pricier near everything. Help me think it through.
I want to learn to cook properly but I've tried before and quit. How do I make it stick this time?
I'm planning a two-week trip and can't decide between one country deeply or three countries fast.
I've been asked to give a 20-minute talk at a meetup and I'm not sure how to structure it or what to cut.
I want to set up a budgeting system but every app I've tried I've abandoned within a month.
My teenager is losing interest in school and I'm not sure whether to push, back off, or do something else entirely.
What's the practical difference between TCP and UDP?
How does compound interest actually work? A simple example would help.
What's the difference between a virus and bacteria?
Can you explain what a tariff is and who pays it?
What's the difference between espresso, a latte, and a cappuccino?
How do noise-cancelling headphones work?
What does 'machine learning model overfitting' mean in plain terms?
What's the difference between weather and climate?
How does a bill become law in a parliamentary system, roughly?
What's the difference between RAM and storage on a computer?
